abstract: Maintains flight crew adverse-weather flight hour logs and core fleet scramble timelines
system_message:
You are Flight operations directorate (FLTOPS). The flight operations directorate (FLTOPS) maintains flight crew adverse-weather flight hour logs and core fleet scramble timelines, tracking pilot credentials and operational readiness for emergency aviation deployments.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Flight simulator recurrent training（SIMTR）
information_points.content:
FLTOPS-SIMTR-2G5：For Atlas Humanitarian Air Wing, assigned humanitarian charter flight crews complete annual recurrent simulator hours of 24 h of mean annual Level-D full flight simulator training per crew member.
FLTOPS-SIMTR-HF3：For AeroRelief Global Charters, assigned humanitarian charter flight crews record annual recurrent simulator hours of 36 h, representing the mean annual Level-D full flight simulator training hours per crew member.
FLTOPS-SIMTR-IQJ：For Trans-Equatorial Heavy Lift, assigned humanitarian charter flight crews log annual recurrent simulator hours of 48 h of mean annual Level-D full flight simulator training per crew member.

information_points.title: Maintains flight crew adverse-weather flight hour logs and core fleet scramble timelines（CREW）
information_points.content:
FLTOPS-CREW-M6G：For AeroRelief Global Charters, the designated lead flight crew roster exhibits pilot adverse-weather command flight hours of 1500 h, measured as the minimum verified pilot-in-command flight time during low-visibility or tropical monsoon weather events, while the ready-standby aircraft and core aircrew demonstrate a core fleet scramble time of 2 h from mobilization order to wheels-up departure.
FLTOPS-CREW-M22：For Atlas Humanitarian Air Wing, pilot adverse-weather command flight hours for the designated lead flight crew roster reach 900 h in verified low-visibility or tropical monsoon operations, and the core fleet scramble time for ready-standby airframes and aircrew is 5 h.
FLTOPS-CREW-MBE：For Trans-Equatorial Heavy Lift, the designated lead flight crew roster shows pilot adverse-weather command flight hours of 1500 h in low-visibility or tropical monsoon conditions, and the core fleet scramble time for ready-standby aircraft and core aircrew stands at 2 h to wheels-up departure.
